security_audit.summary: All 14 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, metadata, configuration documentation, or a rate-limit note. A medium-risk semantic finding remains because the skill directs an agent to run state-changing commands against a physical sleep device through an authenticated unofficial API.

remediation.issue: Commands can change temperature, alarms, audio, power, schedules, and bed position.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before every state-changing command and show the intended target and value.

remediation.issue: Authentication uses a password through configuration or environment variables with an unofficial API client.
remediation.suggestion: Keep credentials out of prompts and logs, restrict configuration permissions, and avoid repeated authentication attempts.

content.user_title: Control Your Eight Sleep Pod with eightctl
content.value_statement: Managing pod temperature, alarms, and schedules through separate controls can be slow. This skill uses eightctl commands to inspect and manage supported Eight Sleep features.
actual_capabilities: Checks the current Eight Sleep pod status.
Turns the pod on or off and sets a requested temperature.
Lists, creates, and dismisses supported alarms.
Lists, creates, and updates supported schedules.
Checks, plays, or pauses supported audio features.
Retrieves base information and adjusts supported base angles.
limitations: The eightctl binary must be installed and authenticated before use.
The underlying API is unofficial and may change or enforce rate limits.
Available commands depend on the installed eightctl version and connected hardware.
State-changing actions require careful confirmation because they affect a physical device.

use_cases.title: Check Bed Status
use_cases.description: Review pod power, temperature, and current settings before sleep without changing the device.

use_cases.title: Manage Sleep Routines
use_cases.description: Create or update alarms and schedules through guided eightctl commands.

use_cases.title: Automate Pod Operations
use_cases.description: Coordinate temperature, audio, and base adjustments within approved automation workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Check Pod Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Eight Sleep pod status with eightctl. Summarize power, temperature, and active settings without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Set Pod Temperature
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare to set my pod temperature to [temperature]. Show the exact change and ask for confirmation before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Review Alarms and Schedules
prompt_templates.prompt: List my current alarms and schedules. Identify conflicts or missing days, but do not change anything.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Device Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pod status, schedules, alarms, audio, and base settings. Propose a bedtime configuration and request confirmation for each state-changing command.

output_examples.input: Check my pod status without changing anything.
output_examples.output: The pod is on. The current temperature target is 20 degrees. No settings were changed.

output_examples.input: Set the pod temperature to 19 degrees.
output_examples.output: The requested change is 19 degrees. Please confirm before I apply this temperature setting.

output_examples.input: Review my alarms and schedules for conflicts.
output: Two alarms are configured for the same morning.
The weekend schedule starts later than the weekday schedule.

best_practices: Check current status before issuing any state-changing command.
Request explicit confirmation for temperature, alarm, schedule, power, audio, or base changes.
Protect credentials and avoid repeated logins that may trigger rate limits.
anti_patterns: Do not place Eight Sleep passwords in prompts, transcripts, or shared logs.
Do not repeat failed authentication attempts or rapid API requests.
Do not change physical device settings without confirming the exact target and value.

faq.question: What must be installed before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install the eightctl command-line tool and configure valid Eight Sleep authentication.

faq.question: Can this skill check status without changing settings?
faq.answer: Yes. It can request pod status and summarize available information without issuing state-changing commands.

faq.question: Can it change pod temperature?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prepare a temperature command, but it should request explicit confirmation before execution.

faq.question: Does it manage alarms and schedules?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports listing and documented create, update, or dismiss operations available through eightctl.

faq.question: Why should repeated logins be avoided?
faq.answer: The unofficial API is rate-limited, so repeated authentication attempts may fail or temporarily restrict access.

faq.question: Does this skill store my credentials?
faq.answer: The skill documents configuration and environment options. Credential storage behavior is controlled by eightctl and your local setup.
